0.1.n: Marks 今日 as the topic of the sentence.

0.2.n: Combines with 月 to name September, the ninth month.

0.3.n: After a number, 月 names a calendar month.

0.4.n: 13日 gives the day of the month, not a duration here.

0.6.n: Names the weekday; the sentence leaves out the usual ending です.

1.0.n: 紹介する is the plain form; here it refers to the upcoming introductions.

1.1.n: Turns 紹介する into a noun-like phrase referring to what will be introduced.

1.2.n: Marks 紹介するの as the topic; the answer comes after the listed headlines.

2.0.n: Refers to bags provided at a store checkout.

2.1.n: Links レジ袋 to 代わり, identifying what is being replaced.

2.2.n: Used in の代わりに to express using something instead of something else.

2.3.n: Completes の代わりに, marking the role of a substitute.

2.4.n: Names reusable Japanese cloths used to wrap and carry items.

2.5.n: Marks 風呂敷 as the thing described as popular.

2.6.n: A noun expressing popularity; headline style leaves out がある or です.

3.0.n: Sets the subject of the quoted headline that follows.

3.2.n: Japanese nouns do not require a plural ending.

3.3.n: Marks 子ども as the people doing the playing.

3.4.n: する means do; the context supplies online games as the activity.

3.5.n: Follows the plain verb する to specify the time of the activity.

3.6.n: Marks the whole when-children-play phrase as the situation being discussed.

3.7.n: Refers to the children's parents; no plural ending is needed.

3.8.n: Marks 親 as the people asked to stay.

3.9.n: Combines with に to describe accompanying the children.

3.10.n: Makes 一緒に describe how the parents should stay.

3.11.n: The て-form of いる ends the quote as a request, with ください left out.

4.0.n: Points back to the two headlines just mentioned.

4.1.n: Combines with つ to count the news items.

4.2.n: A general counting ending; 2つ counts two things without specifying their type.

4.3.n: Links the quantity この2つ to the noun ニュース.

4.4.n: Refers to the two news items listed, rather than news in general.

4.5.n: Politely completes the sentence begun with 紹介するのは in line 1.

5.0.n: Introduces the next planned activity after the news.

5.2.n: Explicitly identifies the speaker as the person who likes the song.

5.3.n: Marks 私 as the person who likes something within the phrase describing 歌.

5.4.n: 好き describes a preference and works like an adjective, not a verb.

5.5.n: Connects 好き to 歌 so the preference describes the song.

5.6.n: 私が好きな before this noun tells us which kind of song the speaker means.

5.7.n: Marks 歌 as what the speaker will introduce.

5.8.n: Politely addresses the audience as a group.

5.9.n: Marks 皆さん as the recipients of the introduction.

5.10.n: The polite ます form of 紹介する describes the speaker's upcoming action.

6.0.n: Signals a transition from the introduction to starting the program.

6.1.n: A conversational version of では, repeated here as a natural spoken transition.

6.3.n: 始める becomes 始めましょう to politely suggest starting together.

0.lit: Today, as for: ninth month, thirteenth day, Sunday.
0.tip: Japanese dates put the month before the day, followed here by the weekday.

1.lit: What I will introduce, as for...
1.tip: Verb + のは sets up what will be identified later; line 4 completes this sentence.

2.lit: In place of checkout bags, wrapping cloths are popular.
2.tip: Aの代わりに means instead of A.

3.lit: Online games: When children play, parents, stay together with them.
3.tip: A verb ending in the て-form can make a request without an explicit ください.

4.lit: These two news stories are it.
4.tip: This line supplies the answer to 紹介するのは: what will be introduced is these two news stories.

5.lit: After that, I will introduce to everyone a song that I like.
5.tip: 私が好きな comes before 歌: Japanese puts descriptions before the noun they describe.

6.tip: The ending ましょう makes a polite suggestion to do something together.
